title: Jerusalem Day Flag March: Tens of Thousands March Through Muslim Quarter Chanting 'Death to Arabs'; 13 Arrested
detail: On May 15, 2026 — Yom Yerushalayim (Jerusalem Day) — tens of thousands of ultranationalist Israeli youth marched through the Muslim Quarter of Jerusalem's Old City in the annual Flag March. Participants chanted 'Death to Arabs,' 'May your village burn,' and 'Mohammed is dead.' National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir stormed the Al-Aqsa compound during the day's festivities, brandishing an Israeli flag and declaring 'The Temple Mount is in our hands.' Palestinian shopkeepers shuttered their stores as ordered by march organizers; residents were barred from entering the Old City. Israeli police arrested 13 individuals. Extremist mobs spat on and assaulted journalists, while marchers chanted racist songs throughout the procession. Jewish-Arab peace coalition Standing Together organized counter-protests. Jordan's Foreign Ministry issued a renewed condemnation. The Flag March, which routes participants deliberately through the predominantly Palestinian Muslim Quarter, is held annually to mark Israel's 1967 reunification of Jerusalem — a development Palestinians and most of the international community view as illegal occupation of East Jerusalem. In 2021, tensions over the march directly preceded the outbreak of Operation Guardian of the Walls. Palestinian human rights organizations documented numerous assaults, verbal abuse incidents, and forced shop closures along the march route.

media.caption: Ultranationalist Israeli marchers chant 'Death to Arabs' through Jerusalem's Muslim Quarter during Jerusalem Day Flag March — May 15, 2026

title: IDF Kills Izz al-Din al-Haddad, Hamas Armed Wing Chief in Gaza — 7 Dead, 50+ Wounded in Rimal Strike
detail: Israeli forces struck an apartment building in the Rimal neighborhood of Gaza City on May 15, 2026, killing Izz al-Din al-Haddad — identified by Israel as the head of Hamas's armed wing (Qassam Brigades) in Gaza and one of the last surviving architects of the October 7, 2023 attacks. A nearby vehicle was also struck in the operation. At least 7 people were killed and more than 50 wounded in the strikes. An Israeli official stated al-Haddad had been 'actively undermining Trump's Gaza plan' by organizing continued militant operations during the October 2025 ceasefire. Hamas initially did not confirm al-Haddad's death on May 15 but a Hamas official confirmed it on May 16, 2026. The killing marks the most senior Hamas military elimination since the October 2025 ceasefire, further complicating Hamas disarmament negotiations. Al-Haddad was one of the last surviving top Qassam commanders remaining in Gaza.

media.caption: IDF strikes Rimal neighborhood of Gaza City on May 15, 2026, killing Hamas armed wing chief Izz al-Din al-Haddad; 7 killed, 50+ wounded

title: IDF Chief Zamir Observes 'Sulfur and Fire' Snap Readiness Drill on Jordan Border; Cites Oct 7 Border Surprise as Key Lesson
detail: IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir observed a snap readiness drill on the Jordanian border on May 15, 2026, code-named 'Sulfur and Fire,' involving the 96th and 80th regional divisions plus special forces. Zamir cited the main lesson of the October 7, 2023 attack as 'the need for a high and constant level of readiness for a surprise attack on our borders.' The drill tested rapid mobilization and multi-division coordination along the Jordan River border — Israel's eastern perimeter. The choice of the Jordanian border is notable given ongoing Jordan-Israel tensions over Palestinian issues: Jordan has been sharply critical of Israeli settler actions and Ben-Gvir's Temple Mount incursions, and Jordanian officials have publicly discussed downgrading ties. The drill also comes amid Israeli awareness that the Jordanian border remains one of the few perimeters with significant irregular crossings — some linked to smuggling arms to the West Bank. The snap exercise with no advance notice to the divisions tested the 'zero warning' readiness paradigm that the Oct 7 attack demonstrated as critically lacking.

media.caption: IDF Chief of Staff Zamir observes 'Sulfur and Fire' snap readiness drill on Jordanian border — May 15, 2026

title: Trump Ends Gulf Tour in UAE Without Visiting Israel; Reiterates Gaza 'Freedom Zone' Plan, Floats 20-Year Iran Nuclear Suspension
detail: President Donald Trump concluded his three-country Gulf tour (Saudi Arabia, Qatar, UAE) on May 15, 2026 without visiting Israel — the first US presidential Middle East trip to exclude Israel since Trump's own 2017 tour included the historic visit to Jerusalem. The omission was widely interpreted as Trump distancing himself from Netanyahu's government during politically sensitive Gulf diplomatic and business dealings. Throughout the tour Trump signed arms deals worth hundreds of billions and investment frameworks, but Israel — which typically features on Middle East presidential itineraries — was conspicuously absent from the stops. Trump reiterated his 'Freedom Zone' proposal for Gaza — a US-managed reconstruction and governance zone — at the GCC Summit in Riyadh, describing it as 'the only viable path to peace and prosperity for Palestinians.' At a business roundtable in Doha, Trump floated the idea of accepting a 20-year suspension of Iran's nuclear program rather than full dismantlement, saying 'Twenty years is enough — a lot can happen in twenty years.' The absence of an Israel leg also underscored the diplomatic strain caused by Netanyahu's ICC arrest warrants, which complicate the Israeli prime minister's own travel, and the impasse over Gaza peace talks. Middle East Eye reported that Trump 'doesn't want Netanyahu to spoil his Gulf visit.' The tour is expected to generate $3.8 trillion in total US-Gulf economic agreements over 10 years, dwarfing any previous Middle East diplomatic package.

media.caption: Trump concludes Gulf tour without visiting Israel; reiterates Gaza 'Freedom Zone' plan and floats 20-year Iran nuclear suspension — May 15, 2026

title: UN Security Council Holds Open Debate: Consolidate Gaza Ceasefire and Halt Escalating West Bank Settlement Violence
detail: The United Nations Security Council held an open debate on May 15, 2026 focused on consolidating the Gaza ceasefire and halting the escalating West Bank settlement activity. The debate, timed to coincide with the 78th Nakba anniversary (May 15), heard statements from dozens of UN member states and key stakeholders. UN officials and member states highlighted the continuing deterioration: 828+ Palestinians killed since the October 2025 ceasefire, ongoing IDF operations inside Gaza, the disarmament negotiation deadlock between Israel and Hamas, UN OCHA's report of a 37% decline in humanitarian aid flow in Q1 2026 despite the ceasefire, and the UN OHCHR's March 2026 report documenting approval of 64,000 new West Bank settlement housing units in a single year. Board of Peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov addressed the Council, reaffirming that Hamas disarmament is 'not negotiable' and describing the ceasefire as 'fragile but holding.' Multiple member states called for resumption of humanitarian access and an immediate settlement freeze. The US used the meeting to reaffirm support for the Trump ceasefire framework while opposing any UNSC resolution that might constrain Israeli operational flexibility. Al Jazeera reported the Gaza toll standing at 72,619 Palestinians killed since October 7, 2023 as of the UNSC debate.

media.caption: UN Security Council holds open debate on consolidating Gaza ceasefire and halting West Bank settlement activity on the 78th Nakba anniversary — May 15, 2026
